title: Normalization tensor decomposition for a local weakly etale map
statement: Let $C$ be a commutative Noetherian universally catenary local domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-exc-excellent-ring], let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(C)$, and let $C'$ be the integral closure of $C$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], finite as a $C$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $D$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring and let $f:C\to D$ be a local weakly etale homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Here a local ring has one maximal ideal, local means its inverse image is the source maximal ideal, and a domain is nonzero with no zero divisors. Then $D$ is reduced (an element whose positive power is zero is zero). Write $Q(D)$ for the total ring of fractions, obtained by inverting every nonzerodivisor of $D$, and $D'$ for the integral closure of $D$ in $Q(D)$. There is a canonical $D$-algebra isomorphism $C'\otimes_C D\cong D'$. For every minimal prime $P$ of $D$ (a prime with no strictly smaller prime), put $E=\overline{D/P}^{\,\operatorname{Frac}(D/P)}$. There is a commutative ring $F$ and a $D$-algebra isomorphism $D'\cong E\times F$ whose projection to $E$ restricts on $D$ to $D\to D/P\hookrightarrow E$. Tensor products have their usual algebra multiplication $(a\otimes b)(a'\otimes b')=aa'\otimes bb'$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Math. J. 60 (1976), 139–149
source.place: Lemma 5.5 proof, first two sentences, printed p. 147 (PDF p. 9): normalization base change cited as [4, Lemma 3.9], followed by the component product decomposition. The weakly etale map to the factor is derived in the item, not included here.

proof.text: Put $S=C\setminus\{0\}$, $T=D\otimes_C K$, and $H=C'\otimes_C D$. Weak etaleness gives flatness of $D$ over $C$ by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. For $s\in S$, multiplication by $s$ on $C$ is injective, so its tensor with $D$ is injective by the explicit injectivity criterion in [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; this is multiplication by $f(s)$ on $D$. Thus $f(S)$ consists of nonzerodivisors. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], $T=f(S)^{-1}D$. The fraction equality in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] now shows $D\to T$ injective: $d/1=0$ implies $f(s)d=0$, hence $d=0$. Applying the same flatness criterion to the inclusion $C'\hookrightarrow K$ gives an injection $H\hookrightarrow K\otimes_C D\cong T$, where the last swap sends $k\otimes d$ to $d\otimes k$ (and swaps back for its inverse).

Base change of $C\to D$ along $C\to K$ is weakly etale by [lem-exc-weakly-etale-ring-base-change-composition]; its target is $T$, up to the pure-tensor swap. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field] with the field $K$: $T$ is reduced and every finitely generated $K$-subalgebra of $T$ is finite etale. Since $D\hookrightarrow T$, any nilpotent of $D$ is zero in $T$ and hence zero in $D$. This proves the reducedness clause of the item.

We identify the ambient ring $T$ with $Q(D)$ without assuming it is a field. If $a$ is a nonzerodivisor of $D$, its image $u=a/1$ is a nonzerodivisor of $T$: from $u(b/f(s))=0$ the localization equality gives $f(t)ab=0$ for some $t\in S$, whence $f(t)b=0$ and $b/f(s)=0$. By Step 2, the subalgebra $K[u]\subset T$ is finite etale. By [lem-sc-finite-etale-algebra-criterion] it is a finite product of fields. In that product every coordinate of $u$ is nonzero: a zero coordinate would give a nonzero coordinate idempotent $e\in K[u]\subset T$ with $ue=0$. Taking the coordinatewise inverses therefore gives an inverse to $u$ in $K[u]$, hence in $T$. Thus every nonzerodivisor of $D$ is a unit in $T$. The two fraction maps are $Q(D)\to T$, $a/b\mapsto(a/1)(b/1)^{-1}$, and $T=f(S)^{-1}D\to Q(D)$, $d/f(s)\mapsto d/f(s)$. They are well-defined by the fraction equality of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], since $f(S)$ consists of nonzerodivisors; they are inverse on fractions and are $D$-algebra maps. Hence $T\cong Q(D)$ canonically.

source.place: Tag 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field) and the localization fraction construction, Tag 07JZ

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal] to the identity finite extension $K/K$. It says precisely that $C'$ is an integrally closed domain and $K$ is its fraction field. Base change of $C\to D$ along $C\to C'$ gives a weakly etale map $C'\to H$ by [lem-exc-weakly-etale-ring-base-change-composition]. Locality or a domain hypothesis on $H$ is not needed here.

The ambient ring in the weak-etale integral-closedness theorem for $C'\to H$ is $H\otimes_{C'}K$. Its explicit isomorphism to $T$ sends $(c'\otimes d)\otimes k$ to $d\otimes(c'k)$ and has inverse $d\otimes k\mapsto(1\otimes d)\otimes k$. Here $c'$ is viewed in $K$. These expressions respect the $C$- and $C'$-balancing relations and multiplication. Their two composites fix each pure tensor, using $(c'\otimes d)\otimes k=(1\otimes d)\otimes c'k$. The tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] therefore gives mutually inverse algebra maps, whose restriction on $H$ is exactly the injection of Step 1.

source.place: Tensor universal property and balancing; compare Tag 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule)

proof.text: Now [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-integral-closure], applied to the integrally closed domain $C'$ with fraction field $K$ and the weakly etale algebra $H$, says that $H$ is integrally closed in $H\otimes_{C'}K$. Step 5 identifies this with the inclusion $H\hookrightarrow T$, so $H$ is integrally closed in $T=Q(D)$.

Every element of $C'$ is integral over $C$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-integral-base-change], and the swap $d\otimes c'\leftrightarrow c'\otimes d$, show that $H$ is integral over $D$. Thus the injection $H\hookrightarrow Q(D)$ has image contained in $D'$. Conversely, if $x\in D'$, a monic polynomial over $D$ annihilating $x$ is also a monic polynomial over $H$, since the inclusion of $D$ in $Q(D)$ factors through $H$ via $d\mapsto1\otimes d$. Integral closedness from Step 6 forces $x\in H$. The two subrings are equal, proving the canonical $D$-algebra isomorphism $C'\otimes_C D\cong D'$. Its map on pure tensors is $c'\otimes d\mapsto c'd$ in $Q(D)$, with $c'$ mapped through $K\to T$.

As $D$ is reduced and Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-noetherian-total-ring-fractions] gives finitely many distinct minimal primes $P_1,\ldots,P_t$ and a canonical $D$-algebra isomorphism $Q(D)\cong\prod_i D_{P_i}$, with $D_{P_i}$ a field and $P_iD_{P_i}=0$. Explicitly $D_{P_i}\cong\operatorname{Frac}(D/P_i)$: the map $D\to D_{P_i}$ kills $P_i$; its kernel is exactly $P_i$, since $sd=0$ with $s\notin P_i$ forces $d\in P_i$. Every nonzero class $\bar s\in D/P_i$ has $s\notin P_i$ and becomes invertible. The maps of fields send $d/s$ to $\bar d/\bar s$ and back. They are well-defined and inverse by the fraction relations of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Write $L_i=\operatorname{Frac}(D/P_i)$ for these factors.

source.place: Tags 02LX (lemma-total-ring-fractions-no-embedded-points) and 00EU (lemma-minimal-prime-reduced-ring); compare morphisms.tex Tag 035P, parts (1)-(2)

proof.text: Put $E_i=\overline{D/P_i}^{\,L_i}$. Under Step 8's isomorphism, a tuple integral over $D$ has integral coordinates over $D/P_i$, by projecting its monic equation. Conversely, for $x_i\in E_i$ choose a monic annihilating polynomial over $D/P_i$ and lift each of its coefficients to $D$, preserving the leading coefficient $1$, to obtain $p_i\in D[X]$. The monic polynomial $p=\prod_i p_i$ annihilates the tuple $(x_i)$: in coordinate $i$ its $p_i$ factor is zero. This finite product proves that the integral closure of $D$ in $\prod_iL_i$ is exactly $\prod_iE_i$, with the same $D$-algebra structure. This uses only the monic-polynomial definition in [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]; in particular it does not apply a theorem about products of base rings to the diagonal base ring $D$.

source.place: Tag 035P (lemma-description-normalization), part (3); explicit coordinatewise monic-polynomial argument

proof.text: For the given minimal prime $P$, choose its index $j$ in the finite list of Step 8 and set $F=\prod_{i\ne j}E_i$ with its induced $D$-algebra structure. The isomorphism of Step 9 followed by the coordinate permutation and grouping $\prod_iE_i\to E_j\times\prod_{i\ne j}E_i$ is a $D$-algebra isomorphism $D'\cong E\times F$. Its first projection sends $d\in D$ to its class modulo $P$ in $E$, since the coordinate maps in Step 8 are precisely the localization and quotient fraction maps. If there is only one minimal prime, the empty product defining $F$ is the zero ring and the same maps apply.

split_report.summary: Replaced the earlier clause-relabelling attempt by ten proof steps using existing DAG inputs only. The proof identifies the generic tensor algebra with total fractions via finite etale subalgebras; proves the normalization equality by weak-etale integral closedness and integrality; and constructs the minimal-prime normalization factors by lifting monic polynomials. Removed all three undelivered proposed children. The item statement and statement dependencies are unchanged.

No chapter or unit route is changed.

tool_uses.why: The generic fibre is weakly etale over K; its reducedness and finite etale finitely generated subalgebras identify its ambient total-fraction ring. This is a general algebra tool, not a replacement of the unit route.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NB-0377c9b2d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 10 steps and the statements of all 18 cited nodes. No new nodes were created and the statement and stmt_deps are unchanged and not weakened. The statement is true; I checked it on a field, a DVR, a non-normal domain with f=id, the reducible ring k[x,y]_(x,y)/(xy) and the one-minimal-prime case (F=0). Step 1: flatness of D over C makes f(S) nonzerodivisors and IsLocalization.tensor gives T=f(S)^{-1}D, so D and H inject into T. Step 2: base change and lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field (matches Stacks 092Q, more-algebra.tex l.30504) make T reduced, hence D reduced. Step 3: K[u] is finite etale, hence a product of fields; a zero coordinate would give an idempotent killed by u, so u is a unit and T=Q(D); I checked well-definedness and inverses of both fraction maps. Steps 4-6: C' is a normal domain with fraction field K, and 092W (l.30728, Lean-closed node) applies to C'->H, with the explicit isomorphism H(x)_{C'}K=T. Step 7: integral base change plus Step 6 gives H=D'. Steps 8-10: Q(D) is the product of D_{P_i}, each D_{P_i}=Frac(D/P_i), and the product of lifted monic polynomials gives prod E_i; the regrouping handles the empty product. The steps marked elementary really are. No duplicate found by rg over dag/nodes: the normalization-dimension, Nagata-ascent, total-fractions and minimal-product nodes all differ.
